memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'"If you make an altar of stones for me, do not build it with dressed stones,
for you will defile it if you use a tool on it. And do not go up to my altar on
steps, or your private parts may be exposed."'" - Ex 20:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two odd-sounding rules close the chapter, and both make sense once we see what
they guard against.

First, no tools on the stones. The moment a craftsman shapes an altar, human
skill enters the picture, and skill invites pride. An unshaped stone is simply
what God made. Nobody can admire the workmanship, because there is none.

That is the point. Salvation and worship rest on what God provides, not on what
we contribute. Paul writes that we are saved by grace through faith, "not by
works, so that no one can boast" (Eph 2:9). No boasting at the altar.

Second, no steps. This was about modesty in an age before tailored clothing, and
underneath it lies a concern for dignity. Worship should never become a display,
and it should never expose or shame anyone.

Both rules point the same direction. Worship is not about the worshipper. Not our
craftsmanship, not our appearance, not our performance.

The chapter that began with God thundering from a mountain ends with instructions
to keep human pride out of the way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there anything in how you worship or serve that is really about being
   seen?
2. What are you tempted to boast about before God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, keep my hands off what only You can do. Let my worship be about You and
never about how I appear. Amen.
